title: Grammar: Capstone review: choose the form that serves the message
subtitle: B1 · Unit 12: B1 · B1 capstone: communicate independently across familiar situations

steps.title: Capstone review: choose the form that serves the message
steps.body: There is no new grammar target in this capstone. Before producing a long answer, decide what the message needs: a clear timeline, a condition, a relative clause, a reported statement, an explanation or a question. Use the simplest accurate form. Keep a person's point of view separate from confirmed information; mark limits instead of inventing certainty. Use connectors to make one relationship clear at a time. In a new setting, repeat a noun when pronouns would make the reference hard to follow.

steps.title: Capstone review: choose the form that serves the message
rows: La salle avait fermé; nous avons trouvé une autre entrée.
The room had closed; we found another entrance.
Si le groupe changeait l'heure, je pourrais participer.
If the group changed the time, I could participate.
La responsable a dit que l'essai était possible, sans confirmer la date.
The coordinator said the trial was possible without confirming the date.

steps.prompt: Which response keeps an unconfirmed proposal uncertain?
options: Le comité a confirmé la date, même si personne ne l'a fait.
Tout le monde a accepté le projet.
Le changement aura lieu demain, c'est sûr.
Le comité étudie l'idée; la date n'est pas confirmée.
steps.explain: This wording reports what is known and marks the missing confirmation.

steps.prompt: What is the best repair when you miss a key detail?
options: Guess and present the guess as fact
Ask the speaker to repeat or clarify it
steps.explain: A direct repair is more reliable than guessing.

steps.prompt: What does a transfer task check?
options: Whether you can use learning in a changed situation
Whether you can repeat one memorized model
steps.explain: Transfer checks use beyond the practiced example.
